data.cultural_impact: The name Tirumala has significant cultural importance in Hinduism, as it is closely associated with Lord Venkateswara, also known as Balaji or Lord Krishna, who resides on the seven hills of Tirumala, located in the Tirupati region of Andhra Pradesh, India. Thousands of pilgrims visit this holy site each year to offer their prayers and seek blessings from the deity.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu philosophy, Tirumala represents the divine abode of Lord Venkateswara, a manifestation of Vishnu, who is regarded as the preserver of the universe. The name is believed to signify purity, divinity, and protection. It is believed that the name Tirumala invokes the blessings of the deity, bringing peace, prosperity, and harmony into one's life. In Hindu prayers and chants, the name Tirumala is used as a form of address to Lord Venkateswara, showing reverence and devotion to the deity.

historical_references.reference: Tirumala is a popular name for Lord Venkateswara in the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam temple in Andhra Pradesh, India.
